transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Thank you so much for fitting me in, it's really wonderful to meet you too. I, um... I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. I'm sure a lot of this is just normal stress—being a chief executive comes with a lot of pressure, and I always just want to make sure I'm doing a good job for everyone. 

But I guess I'm here today because... well, I've been experiencing something a little embarrassing, to be completely honest. I keep hearing people talking about me. Usually it's the board members or my staff. I'll hear them saying things like... like I'm ruining the company. And I hear it coming right through the conference room walls, or even from my cell phone when it's completely turned off. 

It's just that it sounds so incredibly clear to me that I actually answer them back out loud, right there in the room, before I even realize that... well, that no one else heard it. I'm so sorry, I know that probably sounds terrible and strange. Am I making sense? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question correctly.
How long have you been experiencing these auditory perceptions?

Oh, um... well, I really hope it doesn't make me sound too terrible, but... I'd say the voices—the ones coming from the walls or my phone—have been happening for about the past three months. It's really not that long in the grand scheme of things, right? Just a recent little rough patch, I'm sure. I try my absolute best to just work through it so I don't let my team down. 

Is... is three months a normal amount of time for stress to do something like this? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline and answering properly.
During these past three months, have you experienced any periods where your mood was significantly elevated, or where you felt so depressed that you struggled to function?

Oh, no, definitely not. I mean, I hope I'm not misunderstanding what you're asking, but my mood has been... well, very steady, I think. I always try to keep a really positive attitude for my staff, you know? It's so important as a leader to set a good example. 

I haven't had any days where I couldn't function or couldn't get out of bed—I would absolutely hate to let my team down like that, it would be so unprofessional of me. And I haven't felt unusually high or... or hyper, either. Just my normal, everyday self, really, aside from the... the hearing things part. I'm still managing my daily tasks and keeping up with my responsibilities. 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm answering that clearly enough for your notes.

Aside from the voices you hear, do you have any firm beliefs about your staff or colleagues—for instance, do you feel certain that they are actively conspiring against you or plotting to sabotage your position?

Oh, goodness, no. No, definitely not. I... I really hope it doesn't seem like I'm the kind of manager who doesn't trust her team. They're wonderful people, they really are. 

Even when I hear those things—the voices, I mean—I don't actually sit there and think they're secretly plotting to ruin me or... or conspiring to take my job in real life. I know that probably sounds a bit contradictory, hearing them but not believing they're out to get me, but I really do try to see the best in everyone. I'd never want to falsely accuse my staff of sabotage. That would just be an awful thing for a leader to do. 

So, no, I don't have any firm beliefs like that at all. I hope that's the right answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the correct information so you can do your job.

Aside from the voices you hear, have you noticed any other changes, such as feeling less motivated to do things you used to enjoy, or have others mentioned that your way of speaking has become difficult to follow?

Um... well, I really hate to admit this, because it sounds so... so lazy, and I promise you I am absolutely not a lazy person. I hope you don't judge me too harshly for this. 

But... I guess I have noticed a little bit of a change with my motivation. I used to be the person driving every single idea, you know? Always on the phone, calling people after openings, keeping everyone fired up. I just loved it so much. But recently... I don't know, maybe I'm just going through a bit of a tired phase? 

I'll find myself just sitting at my desk for hours, just... staring at the agenda. And I've been so quiet lately, barely speaking to my husband or my staff. It’s like I just feel almost nothing about the work I used to completely love. 

I feel terrible even saying that out loud. A good executive shouldn't act like that, right? I really am trying my hardest to snap out of it and get back to normal. Does that... does that answer your question about the motivation part? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
When you are speaking with your colleagues or family, have they mentioned that they sometimes find it difficult to understand your train of thought or that your sentences seem disjointed?

Oh, no, definitely not. I... I really pride myself on being a clear communicator. It's so important in my role, you know? You can't lead a team if people can't understand what you're trying to say. 

My husband and my staff, they've never mentioned anything like that to me. I mean, I know I said I've been a bit quieter lately, but when I do speak, I always try to make sure I'm being very professional and articulate. I would just be mortified if people thought I wasn't making sense or if my sentences were all jumbled up. That would reflect so poorly on me. 

So, no, nothing like that at all. I hope that's okay? I just really want to reassure you that I'm still communicating well when I need to.
Have you noticed any changes in your personal hygiene or your ability to take care of your daily routines, such as bathing or getting dressed, over these past three months?

Oh, goodness, no. I... I really pride myself on always being presentable. As an executive, you know, appearance is just so important. I would be absolutely mortified if I ever let my hygiene slip or showed up looking disheveled. 

Even with... well, with everything else going on, and feeling a bit tired like I mentioned, I always make sure I shower and dress properly every single morning. I really hope you don't think I'm the type of person to just let myself go. I try very hard to maintain my standards and take care of myself, I promise. 

Is that... is that the kind of routine you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions correctly.
Have your husband or staff members commented on your facial expressions appearing less animated or your voice sounding more monotone than usual lately?

Um... no, no one has said anything like that to me. I mean, I hope they wouldn't think that. I really try to be warm and engaging, especially with my team. It's so important for morale, you know? 

I know I said I've been quiet, and maybe a little less... energetic than my usual self, but I always try to smile and make sure I sound pleasant when I do talk to people. I'd hate for anyone to think I was being cold or flat. That's just not the kind of leader—or wife—I want to be. 

So, I haven't heard any comments like that. I really do try my best to keep a positive face on things, even if I'm feeling a bit drained. Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Before these voices started three months ago, was there any specific, stressful, or upsetting event that happened in your life?

Um... no, not really. I mean, there wasn't any big crisis or anything like that. Things were actually going quite well, I thought. Work is always busy, of course, being an executive, but it's a good kind of busy. I'm very used to handling it. 

I don't think there was anything unusually stressful or upsetting right before... before all this started. My husband and I have a wonderful relationship, and everything at home was perfectly fine. I try very hard to manage my stress and not let things get to me, so I wouldn't say anything pushed me over the edge or anything like that. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have a specific event to point to? I just wouldn't want you to think I can't handle my responsibilities or that I let stress get the better of me. Is it normal for this to happen without a big trigger?
Have you noticed yourself acting in ways that might seem odd to others, such as doing things that don't seem to have a clear purpose or goal?

Well... um... I suppose there have been a few moments. I really hate to admit this, because I know how important it is to be professional, especially in my position. But... well, sometimes in meetings or at gallery events, I've caught myself doing things that... might seem a little unusual to others. 

Like, I might suddenly stand up, or start rearranging the pens or name cards on the table into these very specific patterns. Or... or sometimes I'll repeat a phrase someone just said, or even hold my hands up in the air like I'm presenting something, when it's not my turn to speak. 

I always realize afterward that it probably didn't make any sense for the room, and I feel so embarrassed. I really try to catch myself, I promise. I don't want anyone to think I'm not paying attention or that I'm being disruptive. I hope you don't think too poorly of me for that... is it okay that I'm sharing this with you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you ever been told by a doctor that you have a medical condition, or have you recently taken any new medications or substances, that might explain why you are hearing these voices?

Um... no, no doctor has ever mentioned anything like that to me. I've always been very healthy, thankfully. I try to take good care of myself, you know, eating right and staying active when I can. 

And as for medications or... or substances... oh goodness, no. I would never take anything that wasn't prescribed, and I haven't started any new medications recently. I know how important it is to keep a clear head, especially with my responsibilities at the gallery. I'd never do anything to jeopardize my work or my health. 

So, there's no medical reason or... or anything I've taken that would cause this. At least, nothing I know of. I hope that's a good thing? I mean, I want to be as helpful as possible so we can figure this out. Did I answer that the right way for you?

You mentioned these experiences began three months ago; have you ever had any similar periods of hearing voices or acting in these unusual ways in the past, even years ago, or has this been the only time in your life?

Um... no, never. This is... this is really the very first time anything like this has ever happened to me. I've always prided myself on being very grounded and put together, you know? In my twenties and thirties, I was so focused on my career and... well, I never had any periods where I heard things or acted out of the ordinary at all. 

I've always been very stable and reliable for my team at the gallery. This whole experience over the last three months has just been so... completely out of character for me, which is why it's so embarrassing to even talk about. I really hope you believe me when I say this is the only time it's ever happened. 

Is it... is it a good sign that I haven't had this happen before? I just really want to do whatever is right so I can get back to being my normal, professional self. I hope that's the answer you were looking for?
Looking back at the past six months, have you felt that your ability to interact with others or perform your job duties has been consistently lower than it was before these past three months?

Oh... um... well, that's a really difficult question to answer. I... I want to be completely honest with you, even though it's incredibly embarrassing to admit. 

I'm usually so on top of everything at the gallery, but... lately, I suppose things have been a little harder. I haven't been as reliable when it comes to running my division. I've been having some trouble keeping up with basic executive decisions, which is just so unlike me. My senior staff—who are just wonderful, by the way—have had to quietly step in and take over a lot of the work I used to handle all by myself. I feel just terrible about it, but I promise I'm trying my absolute hardest to get back to my normal pace.

And... well, at home it's kind of the same story, I'm afraid. My husband has been an absolute saint, but he's had to manage almost all of the household responsibilities recently. I just... I keep leaving things half-finished, or sometimes I just can't seem to start them at all. 

I really hope you don't think I'm just being lazy or incompetent. I hate being a burden to my husband or my team, and I want to do better, I really do. Is it... is it helpful that I'm telling you this? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture so we can fix it. I hope I'm answering this the way you need me to?
Looking back at the six months before these voices started, were you already feeling that your motivation or energy levels were significantly lower than your usual baseline?

Oh... um... well, looking back before all of this really started... I suppose maybe things were already slipping a little bit. It's so hard to admit this, because I really pride myself on being such a go-getter. 

I used to be the person driving every single idea, you know? I was always the one calling people right after our gallery openings to follow up and keep the momentum going. But... well, I guess for a while now, even before the last three months, I've just been finding myself sitting at my desk for hours, just staring at the agenda. I don't mean to be unproductive, I just... I can't seem to get going. 

And I barely speak to my husband or my staff anymore, which is awful of me. The hardest part to say out loud—and I really hope you don't think less of me for this—is that I just feel almost nothing about the work I used to absolutely love. It's like the spark just quietly went out. 

I'm so sorry, I know that sounds terrible and lazy. I really want to care again, I promise I do. Does... does that make sense? Is that the kind of information you were looking for?
